query: How do reasons for visit relate to urgency and visit duration across department and age group?

per_column.name: visit_complexity
per_column.rationale: Ordinal, interpretable categories (Low/Moderate/High) that can be segmented and compared against visit duration; a natural driver of duration. However the distribution is heavily skewed (High=222 vs Moderate=5), so the Moderate/Low buckets are near-empty and limit meaningful comparison, though High vs rest still yields signal.

per_column.name: symptom_category
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, human-readable clinical categories (pain, infection, chronic_condition, etc.) that meaningfully decompose the free-text reason_for_visit into groupable segments. Excellent for cross-tabbing duration/urgency by symptom type; some categories are thin but the top ones support real comparison.

per_column.name: has_procedure
per_column.rationale: Clean, well-balanced binary (Yes=140/No=110) representing an external associational fact plausibly linked to longer visits; ideal for a two-group duration comparison.

judge.rationale: All three columns are external, interpretable segmentation variables rather than restatements of visit_duration_min, and each can be grouped against the focus to reveal relationships. symptom_category and has_procedure are strong: balanced/well-separated and directly derived from the query's reason_for_visit angle. visit_complexity is conceptually apt but its extreme skew (Moderate=5, Low=23) weakens comparative power. As a set they support genuine exploratory analysis of how visit reasons relate to duration, so informativeness is moderately high but capped by the imbalance.
